speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in light of the Auditor-General's Report for FY 2019/2020, (a) whether the Ministry will be undertaking a more wide-scale review of the number of successful career conversions and Professional Conversion Programme outcomes thus far; and (b) what will be the extent of sample checks to be conducted on grant Programme Partners by Workforce Singapore or the Ministry in future.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A significant majority of our PCP participants have enjoyed good employment outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Auditor-General's Office (AGO)’s audit findings do not call into question the impact of these programmes on the participants, but have highlighted issues with the practices of WSG’s programme partners and its supervision of them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There was no doubt that the training had been properly carried out but AGO noted that programme partners had not documented how the participants’ previous and current job scopes were different, which is the requirement for the training to be supported under the PCP.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: WSG has reviewed each of these cases and verified that all 15 participants changed their job scopes and successfully converted into new job roles through their respective PCPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, to address the AGO's concern about the adequacy of its guidelines, WSG will be developing a new PCP guide for all its programme partners by the end of the year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The document will include guidelines on how career conversion should be consistently assessed, as well as the critical information that programme partners should report to ensure better and consistent monitoring of PCP outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: AGO also checked 16 PCPs managed by eight programme partners and found inadequate monitoring of programme outcomes for 10 PCPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The programme partners did not collect the complete set of performance indicators required by WSG and also had varying practices in collecting the information.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: WSG has since reviewed and streamlined its approach.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Henceforth, programme partners will focus on the most important outcome indicators, namely, the number of placements and number of participants who completed training, both of which are straightforward to monitor and report.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond the cases studied by AGO, WSG, on its own, initiated a comprehensive check of over 15,000 placements for similar lapses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is the entire universe of PCP placements since 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Although the review will only be fully completed this year, WSG has not uncovered further lapses or systemic anomalies thus far.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: WSG has reiterated to all programme partners the need to adhere to the PCP administration process, including assessment of career conversion for participants, as well as the importance of close tracking and timely reporting of key programme outcome indicators.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: WSG remains committed to working closely with its programme partners to ensure sound governance and effectiveness of PCPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will also continue to strengthen its supervision over them.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The PCP programme, as carried out under WSG, is a critical one to ensure that Singaporeans, especially PMETs, get into good jobs, and to that end, I think all of us have a deep interest in the programmes' success.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I believe Minister covered it in her reply, where a test check – and AGO cannot check every case; they do test checks – and the test check revealed that 11 out of 56 cases found that there was inadequate verification of career conversion for trainees.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The AGO also noted cases "where the trainees' previous and current job scope appeared to be similar".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My specific questions are which were the three programme partners identified in the AGO Report?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Minister, I believe, in her reply mentioned that there is an on-going review of all PCP matters.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: How prevalent is the problem of a similar job scope, after a PMET worker has undertaken a PCP programme?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He acknowledged their importance and raised the question of the findings by the AGO on the career conversion.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should emphasise this – the AGO noted that the career conversion was not well documented but it did not say that there was no career conversion.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And, on subsequent checks, WSG established the clear fact that there was career conversion and it was a question of the programme partner not having properly documented this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it was not that the job scopes did not change substantially.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It was simply the fact that the programme partners did not document them properly and they did not have a very consistent way of assessing the degree of career conversion and the degree of change of the job scopes across different programme partners.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would just want to emphasise this that there was, in fact, the change in job scope.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: WSG's verification confirmed this and it was a question of documentation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That being the case, we focus on fixing the problem of documentation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And I think I have explained earlier on in my reply how we go about doing so.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I would assume, having read the AGO Report that there would have been some time for WSG to respond, as the Minister has in Parliament, in the AGO Report as to that particular matter of documentation – that, really, it is not that the outcome was not achieved but the documentation was not done properly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My query is, was there enough time for WSG to inform the AGO that it is looking into these findings of the AGO and, thereafter, the reply could have been in the AGO Report?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second question was, as part of my original Supplementary Question, was about the identities of the three programme partners.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the AGO Report, if we look at its reporting of findings in other Ministries, it is quite consistent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the appropriate juncture, their identities will be made public.
